entry.title: Everyday JSON in Java
entry.summary: JSON is ubiquitous in modern software, and many use cases are just too small to justify adding external dependencies. To address these everyday use cases, a new JEP proposes a simple, incubating API for parsing, navigating, and generating JSON documents-both for Java developers and for the JDK itself. While the Java ecosystem offers many libraries with JSON-processing capabilities, this built-in API is not intended to replace them, but rather to offer a low-friction option when an external library would be unnecessary or impractical. In this talk, we will show how Data-Oriented Programming helps simplify the API, discuss its intended use cases, outline the design trade-offs, and demonstrate its capabilities.

entry.title: Structured Concurrency Looms
entry.summary: Structured Concurrency is the next major feature from Project Loom. In this session, we will explain the motivation and design of structured concurrency, show how to use it effectively, and discuss the lessons learned as the feature evolved. We'll also look beneath the surface at the new lower-level API behind the latest design, offering an early glimpse of work that is expected to form the basis of a future lower-level structured concurrency API.

entry.title: Java - The Year of the Runtime!
entry.summary: As AI coding agents make language syntax less central, runtime performance and operability become increasingly important. This keynote explores why Java’s JVM and standard library are well suited to this shift: newer JDKs continually improve performance, observability, garbage collection, and usability while preserving the programming model, with major innovations underway in Projects Valhalla, Leyden, and Lilliput.

entry.title: Agent Helidon: License to Scale
entry.summary: While AI agents are rapidly advancing, the performance and scalability of the agents and their underlying services have received too little attention. This session showcases Helidon powering scalable services via Virtual Thread–based MCP servers and high-performance agents through its compile-time integration with LangChain4j.
